V12-AFP_RESPONSE.title: Alpha-Fetoprotein Decrease from > 1,000 to < 500 ng/mL in Patients with Hepatocellular Carcinoma Leads to Improved Posttransplant Outcomes.
V12-AFP_RESPONSE.locator: Main PDF pp 3–9; Tables 1–3 and Figures 1–3.
V12-AFP_RESPONSE.note: Five-year post-LT OS: 48.8% with final AFP >1000, 67.0% at 101–499, and 88.4% at ≤100. Corresponding Kaplan–Meier recurrence estimates: 35.0%, 13.3%, and 7.2%. The 500–1000 group had only 17 patients. Differences between ≤100 and 101–499 were not statistically significant. Recipient-only, selected historical cohort; treatment and waiting time differed substantially between groups. Non-HCC death was censored for recurrence. No proof that forcing AFP lower causes benefit, no AFP-only/imaging-complete-response subgroup, and no LDLT validation. V12-AFP_500.title: Lower Alpha-Fetoprotein Threshold of 500 ng/mL for Liver Transplantation May Improve Posttransplant Outcomes in Patients With Hepatocellular Carcinoma.

V12-AFP_500.note: Five-year OS at final AFP <100 / 100–499 / ≥500: 72.7% / 70.4% / 56.1%; recurrence: 13.1% / 18.7% / 24.2%. Final AFP ≥500: adjusted mortality HR 1.50 (95% CI 1.07–2.10), recurrence HR 1.88 (1.13–3.14). Historical recipient-only study, not a comparison of transplant versus no transplant. Many had only one AFP. In the ≥500 subgroup, 40.4% were ≥1000; small subgroups cannot establish equivalence. Recurrence estimates censor competing death. Full PDF saved privately; TMC: https://libkey.io/libraries/480/10.1002/lt.26392

V12-AFP_SLOPE.title: Alpha-Fetoprotein Slope >7.5 ng/mL per Month Predicts Microvascular Invasion and Tumor Recurrence After Liver Transplantation for Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
V12-AFP_SLOPE.locator: Main PDF pp 2–6; Tables 1–4 and Figure 1.
V12-AFP_SLOPE.note: AFP slope >7.5 ng/mL/month: adjusted recurrence HR 3.0 (1.1–8.1), microvascular invasion OR 6.8 (1.6–28.7). Five-year recurrence-free probability 69.8% versus 87.4%; survival without recurrence 59.5% versus 75.3%. These are different endpoints, neither pair should be labeled overall survival. Small, data-selected cutoff group; no prospective hold/release validation. The long-term fitted slope cannot be inferred reliably from two closely spaced noisy results. Death was censored for recurrence-free probability. Full PDF saved privately; TMC: https://libkey.io/libraries/480/10.1097/TP.0000000000002094

V12-AFP_NYCA.title: Dynamic α-Fetoprotein Response and Outcomes After Liver Transplant for Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
V12-AFP_NYCA.locator: Main PDF pp 1–8; Table 1, Figures 1–3. Trailing commentary is not a separate reviewed study.
V12-AFP_NYCA.note: Five-year competing-risk cumulative recurrence: 9.5%, 20.5%, 40.5% for low/intermediate/high NYCA categories. Discrimination C statistic 0.66. These are composite-score categories, not isolated AFP ranges. Recipient selection, exclusion of early deaths, no waitlist dropout or transplant-benefit comparison. Maximum-to-final AFP can miss a rebound below the original peak. Extreme-AFP response subgroup was tiny. Full PDF saved privately; TMC: https://libkey.io/libraries/480/10.1001/jamasurg.2021.0954

V12-AFP_OCCULT.title: Management and Prognosis of HCC Patients With Elevated Tumor Markers but no Imaging Recurrence After Radiofrequency Ablation.

Local curative treatment 83.5% versus 78.8% and post-recurrence OS 3.55 versus 3.31 years for detection ≤180 versus >180 days; differences were not statistically significant. RFA-specific, repeated episodes and competing losses; no LT cohort or tested optimal recall interval. Routine imaging is described as every four months in methods versus quarterly in abstract. Case-level AFP discrepancy between Figure 3 and Table 4 is not used. Full PDF saved privately; TMC: https://libkey.io/libraries/480/10.1002/cam4.71812

Historical placebo comparison, not a comparison with current ICI combinations. Grade 3 diarrhea and hand–foot reaction each 8%; dose interruptions/reductions frequent. V12-ASCO_BTC.note: Broad tissue DNA/RNA profiling, MMR and HER2 testing at diagnosis. For eligible MSS/pMMR disease: GemCis plus durvalumab or pembrolizumab (high-quality/strong); GemCis without ICI if unsuitable (conditional). After progression without an actionable target: FOLFOX plus active symptom control or active symptom control alone (conditional). For oxaliplatin-ineligible patients, irinotecan/nal-IRI-based options have low-quality conditional support, not equal default status. Rare targets often rely on small basket cohorts. Grade ≥3 events 71% versus 50%; treatment-related serious events 33% versus 2%. Small phase II trial; subsequent therapy differed (more control patients received later therapy). V12-CASSANDRA.title: Preoperative mFOLFIRINOX versus PAXG for stage I–III resectable and borderline resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PACT-21 CASSANDRA): results of the first randomisation analysis of a randomised, open-label, 2 × 2 factorial phase 3 trial

LRT-27284477.title: Conformal external beam radiation or selective internal radiation therapy-a comparison of treatment outcomes for hepatocellular carcinoma.
LRT-27284477.locator: J Gastrointest Oncol. 2016. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-27284477.note: Retrospective registry analysis. SEER 2004–2011; 189 unresectable HCC patients, SIRT 77 versus coded SBRT 112. Adjusted OS HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.49–1.07) for SIRT versus SBRT; no significant difference. Older registry radiation coding and missing liver-function/dosimetry details limit applicability to modern RS versus SBRT. No equivalence conclusion. LRT-25443863.title: Pilot randomized trial of selective internal radiation therapy vs. chemoembolization in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma.
LRT-25443863.locator: Liver Int. 2015. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-25443863.note: Randomized pilot (SIRTACE). 28 unresectable HCC patients: single-session SIRT 13 versus repeated TACE 15. DCR 76.9% versus 73.3%; no significant difference in 12-week health-related quality of life. Safety/QoL pilot, not powered for survival or transplant endpoints. Complements, rather than confirms, PREMIERE and TRACE. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.

LRT-25373796.title: Randomized comparison of selective internal radiotherapy (SIRT) versus drug-eluting bead transarterial chemoembolization (DEB-TACE) for the treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma.
LRT-25373796.locator: Cardiovasc Intervent Radiol. 2015. Abstract verified; full-text review is incomplete.
LRT-25373796.note: Randomized pilot. 24 predominantly BCLC-B HCC patients: SIRT versus DEB-TACE, 12 per arm. Median PFS 180 versus 216 days; OS 592 versus 788 days; neither difference significant. Four liver-failure deaths occurred after SIRT. Small trial with older delivery/dosimetry; no class-wide Y90 survival advantage. Abstract verified; full-text review is incomplete.

LRT-33687130.title: Randomized controlled study to examine the efficacy of hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy with cisplatin before radiofrequency ablation for hepatocellular carcinoma.
LRT-33687130.locator: Hepatol Res. 2021. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-33687130.note: Randomized study. 70 early HCC patients: cisplatin HAIC before RFA versus RFA alone, 35 per arm. 3-year RFS 54.3% versus 34.3%; HR 0.597 (95% CI 0.320–1.091), p=0.094. Primary RFS endpoint was not significant. A secondary distant-intrahepatic recurrence signal does not establish routine HAIC addition or HAIC as a replacement for ablation. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-33687130.author: Oyama A

LRT-35993224.title: Hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy and sequential ablation treatment in large hepatocellular carcinoma.
LRT-35993224.locator: Int J Hyperthermia. 2022. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-35993224.note: Retrospective, IPTW. 228 HCC patients with tumors >5 cm: HAIC followed by ablation 93 versus HAIC alone 135. Reported 2-year OS: 74.3% versus 27.7%. IPTW and 6-month landmark analyses favored HAIC followed by ablation. Selected HAIC responders; substantial selection bias. Reported survival medians conflict with Results/Figure 2 and are omitted. Tests adding ablation after HAIC, not replacing ablation with HAIC. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-35993224.author: You H

LRT-29631810.title: Sorafenib plus low-dose cisplatin and fluorouracil hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy versus sorafenib alone in patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (SILIUS): a randomised, open label, phase 3 trial.
LRT-29631810.locator: Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol. 2018. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-29631810.note: Randomized phase III (SILIUS). 206 advanced HCC patients; low-dose cisplatin/5-FU HAIC plus sorafenib versus sorafenib. Median OS 11.8 versus 11.5 months; HR 1.009 (95% CI 0.743–1.371), p=0.955. Negative OS trial. Regimen differs from FOLFOX-HAIC trials; increased hematologic toxicity. Do not generalize a benefit across all HAIC regimens. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-29631810.author: Kudo M

LRT-40709764.title: Hepatic Artery Infusion Chemotherapy Compared to Transarterial Radioembolization For Unresectable Colorectal Liver Metastases.
LRT-40709764.locator: Ann Surg. 2025. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-40709764.note: Retrospective multicenter, propensity matched. 708 HAI versus 481 TARE patients; matched within prior systemic-therapy lines. TARE-versus-HAI mortality HR: 1 prior line 1.46 (95% CI 1.02–2.08); 2 lines 1.96 (1.32–2.89); 3–4 lines 0.88 (0.57–1.35). HAI came from one high-volume center, TARE from five others. More subsequent systemic therapy/resection after HAI; treatment and center effects cannot be separated. Not a comparison with ablation. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-40709764.author: Saadat LV

LRT-29181682.title: Effectiveness of Hepatic Artery Infusion (HAI) Versus Selective Internal Radiation Therapy (Y90) for Pretreated Isolated Unresectable Colorectal Liver Metastases (IU-CRCLM).
LRT-29181682.locator: Ann Surg Oncol. 2018. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-29181682.note: Retrospective comparison. 97 pretreated liver-only CRLM patients: HAI 48 versus Y90 49, with modern systemic therapy. Median OS from isolated unresectable diagnosis: 31.2 versus 16.3 months (p<0.001). From initial stage IV diagnosis: 34.4 versus 32.0 months (p=0.291). Retrospective, 97 patients. Survival time origin changes the apparent comparison; treatment timing, subsequent therapy and selection limit causal interpretation. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-29181682.author: Dhir M

LRT-11843249.title: Randomised trial of SIR-Spheres plus chemotherapy vs. chemotherapy alone for treating patients with liver metastases from primary large bowel cancer.
LRT-11843249.locator: Ann Oncol. 2001. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-11843249.note: Randomized phase III. 74 patients with bilobar unresectable CRLM: Y90 plus regional FUDR versus regional FUDR alone. Tumor-volume response 50% versus 24% (p=0.03); liver progression was delayed. Tests adding Y90 to HAI, not Y90 versus HAI alone. Older chemotherapy era; no established overall-survival benefit. Not evidence against ablation of small lesions. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-11843249.author: Gray B

LRT-31177151.title: Comparison of Response and Outcomes of Drug-eluting Bead Chemoembolization (DEB-TACE) Versus Radioembolization (TARE) for Patients With Colorectal Cancer Liver Metastases.
LRT-31177151.locator: Anticancer Res. 2019. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-31177151.note: Retrospective, propensity matched. 202 CRLM patients; 44 matched pairs, DEB-TACE versus TARE. Adjusted OS association for DEB-TACE: HR 0.94 (95% CI 0.54–1.65), p=0.83; toxicity trend 27% versus 9.1%, p=0.057. No significant survival difference; baseline burden and extrahepatic disease varied. Not an equivalence trial. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-31177151.author: Mokkarala M

LRT-41118066.title: Treatment Intensification with Hepatic Arterial Infusion Chemotherapy in Patients with Liver-Only Colorectal Metastases Still Unresectable After Systemic Induction Chemotherapy: Exploratory Findings From a Prematurely Closed Multicenter Randomized Phase II Study: SULTAN UCGI 30/PRODIGE 53 (NCT03164655).
LRT-41118066.locator: Ann Surg Oncol. 2026. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-41118066.note: Prematurely closed randomized phase II (SULTAN). Persistently unresectable liver-only CRLM after systemic induction; 11 HAI-oxaliplatin plus systemic versus 9 systemic alone randomized. Conversion to resection/ablation 7/11 (64%) versus 2/9 (22%), p=0.09; PFS 12.6 versus 4.37 months. Very small, early-closed trial; conversion endpoint not significant. Supports further study, not a confirmed conversion advantage or direct comparison against ablation. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-41118066.author: Boilève A

LRT-39644535.title: Safety and efficacy of adjuvant FOLFOX/FOLFIRI with versus without hepatic arterial infusion of floxuridine in patients following colorectal cancer liver metastasectomy (HARVEST trial): A randomized controlled trial.
LRT-39644535.locator: Eur J Cancer. 2025. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-39644535.note: Prematurely stopped randomized trial (HARVEST). 92 randomized after CRLM surgery; modified ITT 77, HAI-FUDR plus systemic 38 versus systemic 39. 3-year RFS 31.4% versus 34.4%, p=0.28. Stopped for FUDR supply shortage; primary endpoint negative. Exploratory early-RFS/subgroup signals do not establish routine postoperative HAI. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-39644535.author: Wang DS

LRT-42018958.title: Postoperative Hepatic Arterial Infusion With Oxaliplatin After Surgery of Four or More Colorectal Liver Metastases: A Randomized Phase II Trial.
LRT-42018958.locator: J Clin Oncol. 2026. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-42018958.note: Randomized phase II. 99 patients after resection/ablation of ≥4 CRLM: HAI-oxaliplatin 50 versus IV oxaliplatin 49, both with IV LV5FU2. Hepatic RFS 25 versus 12 months, HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.40–0.99); OS HR 0.61 (0.33–1.12), not significant. Grade 3–4 AEs 58% versus 32%. Selected adjuvant setting after complete local treatment of ≥4 CRLM. Phase II design amended before database lock; early closure and immature OS limit certainty. Oxaliplatin infusion is not FUDR pump therapy. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-42018958.author: Gelli M

LRT-42829779.title: Microwave ablation versus stereotactic body radiotherapy for oligometastatic colorectal liver metastases (LAVA-CRLM): a prospective, randomised, phase II trial.
LRT-42829779.locator: Lancet Reg Health Eur. 2026. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-42829779.note: Randomized phase II (LAVA-CRLM). 1–3 CRLM, each ≤4 cm and suitable for both treatments; 100 randomized, 92 modified ITT. 1-year freedom from local progression: MWA 77.7% versus SBRT 83.0%; HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.43–1.74), p=0.70. Grade ≥2 toxicity 25% versus 3%. No demonstrated local-control difference; wide CI and postrandomization exclusions. No survival/noninferiority claim. Grade ≥3 toxicity occurred only after MWA, including one treatment-related death. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-42829779.author: Risumlund SL

LRT-33868997.title: Survival Comparisons of Hepatic Arterial Infusion Chemotherapy With mFOLFOX and Transarterial Chemoembolization in Patients With Unresectable Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma.
LRT-33868997.locator: Front Oncol. 2021. Available main text checked for the stated results.
LRT-33868997.note: Retrospective cohort. 126 unresectable iCCA patients; mFOLFOX-HAIC versus TACE. 1-year OS 60.2% versus 42.9%; 2-year OS 38.7% versus 29.4% (OS comparison p=0.028). PFS did not differ significantly. Nonrandomized, regional catheter regimen. Does not establish pump-FUDR superiority or replace contemporary systemic therapy. Available main text checked for the stated results.
LRT-33868997.author: Cai Z

LRT-40216615.title: Hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy versus transarterial chemoembolization in patients with unresectable intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
LRT-40216615.locator: Eur Radiol. 2025. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-40216615.note: Retrospective multicenter cohort. 181 patients: HAIC 24, conventional TACE 73, DEB-TACE 84. HAIC versus conventional TACE median OS 10.3 versus 5.1 months (p=0.0042); no significant HAIC-versus-DEB-TACE difference reported. Very small HAIC cohort; treatment selection and TACE formulation matter. Do not generalize the comparison to all arterial therapy. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-40216615.author: Zhang Y

LRT-35544131.title: Comparison of Hepatic Arterial Infusion Pump Chemotherapy vs Resection for Patients With Multifocal Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma.
LRT-35544131.locator: JAMA Surg. 2022. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-35544131.note: Retrospective comparison. 319 multifocal iCCA patients: unresectable HAIP-FUDR 141 versus resection 178 across different centers/eras. Median OS 20.3 versus 18.9 months; adjusted HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.55–1.03), p=0.07. HAIP patients had substantially more bilobar/multifocal disease. Not an equivalence trial or reason to deny resection to an otherwise suitable patient; does not distinguish all satellites from metastases. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-35544131.author: Franssen S

LRT-37814188.title: Gemcitabine with Cisplatin Versus Hepatic Arterial Infusion Pump Chemotherapy for Liver-Confined Unresectable Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma.
LRT-37814188.locator: Ann Surg Oncol. 2024. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-37814188.note: Retrospective cross-center cohort. 268 liver-confined unresectable iCCA patients: HAIP ± systemic 192 versus gemcitabine/cisplatin 76. Median OS 27.7 versus 11.8 months; approximately one third of HAIP patients alive at 3 years. Nonrandomized center, era and treatment-line differences; 71.9% of HAIP patients also received systemic treatment. Comparator predates current chemoimmunotherapy; not HAI versus Y90 or ablation. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-37814188.author: Franssen S

LRT-30191056.title: Chemoembolization versus radioembolization for the treatment of unresectable intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma in a single institution image-based efficacy and comparative toxicity.

LRT-30191056.note: Retrospective cohort. 40 unresectable iCCA patients: Y90 25 versus chemoembolization 15. Table 3 disease control: Y90 12/25 (48%) versus chemoembolization 7/15 (47%); no significant difference. Survival was not assessed. Small retrospective cohort. LRT-30191056.author: Akinwande O

LRT-31517072.title: Stereotactic body radiation therapy is associated with improved overall survival compared to chemoradiation or radioembolization in the treatment of unresectable intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
LRT-31517072.locator: Clin Transl Radiat Oncol. 2019. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-31517072.note: Retrospective NCDB comparison. Main-text analysis: SBRT 27, chemoradiation 54, TARE 60; nonmetastatic node-negative unresected iCCA. LRT-42433279.note: Prospective nonrandomized cohort. 127 advanced pCCA patients after biliary drainage: catheter HAIC 63 versus best supportive care 64; preserved reserve, no distant/N2 disease. Median OS 17.63 versus 6.10 months. Patient preference/clinical selection; no contemporary systemic-therapy comparator. LRT-32032719.author: Egger ME

LRT-28677067.title: Intra-arterial therapy of neuroendocrine tumour liver metastases: comparing conventional TACE, drug-eluting beads TACE and yttrium-90 radioembolisation as treatment options using a propensity score analysis model.

LRT-28677067.note: Retrospective, propensity analysis. 192 GEP-NET patients: cTACE 122, DEB-TACE 26, Y90 44. Propensity-weighted median OS: cTACE versus Y90 34.0 versus 22.9 months (p=0.032); cTACE versus DEB-TACE 33.8 versus 23.4 months (p=0.04). Retrospective pairwise weighting across a long treatment era. These adjusted medians differ from the unadjusted three-group medians. Residual confounding prevents a definitive modality ranking. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-28677067.author: Do Minh D

LRT-33004146.title: Chronic Hepatotoxicity in Patients with Metastatic Neuroendocrine Tumor: Transarterial Chemoembolization versus Transarterial Radioembolization.
LRT-33004146.locator: J Vasc Interv Radiol. 2020. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-33004146.note: Retrospective survivor cohort. NELM patients surviving ≥1 year: TACE 63 versus TARE 28; chronic grade ≥3 hepatic toxicity beginning ≥6 months after treatment. Chronic hepatic toxicity: 22% versus 29%. Injury attributed solely to embolotherapy: 3% versus 14% (p=0.07), with more clinical decompensation after TARE. Retrospective survivor-selected cohort. Most TACE toxicities coincided with progression. This cannot estimate toxicity in all treated patients or establish equivalent safety. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-33004146.author: Currie BM

LRT-42006283.title: Yttrium-90 Radioembolization Versus Transarterial Embolization for Lung Carcinoid Hepatic Metastasis.
LRT-42006283.locator: JTO Clin Res Rep. 2026. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-42006283.note: Retrospective single-center cohort. 30 lung-carcinoid patients, 53 primary embolization procedures; Y90 versus bland TAE. Local progression-free survival 30.57 versus 13.9 months (p=0.01); OS 43.5 versus 40.6 months (p=0.49). V12-AFP_RESPONSE.title: Alpha-Fetoprotein Decrease from > 1,000 to < 500 ng/mL in Patients with Hepatocellular Carcinoma Leads to Improved Posttransplant Outcomes.
V12-AFP_RESPONSE.locator: Main PDF pp 3–9; Tables 1–3 and Figures 1–3.
V12-AFP_RESPONSE.note: Five-year post-LT OS: 48.8% with final AFP >1000, 67.0% at 101–499, and 88.4% at ≤100. Corresponding Kaplan–Meier recurrence estimates: 35.0%, 13.3%, and 7.2%. The 500–1000 group had only 17 patients. Differences between ≤100 and 101–499 were not statistically significant. Recipient-only, selected historical cohort; treatment and waiting time differed substantially between groups. Non-HCC death was censored for recurrence. No proof that forcing AFP lower causes benefit, no AFP-only/imaging-complete-response subgroup, and no LDLT validation. Full PDF saved privately; TMC: https://libkey.io/libraries/480/10.1002/hep.30413

V12-AFP_500.title: Lower Alpha-Fetoprotein Threshold of 500 ng/mL for Liver Transplantation May Improve Posttransplant Outcomes in Patients With Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
V12-AFP_500.locator: Main PDF pp 4–9; Tables 1–3 and Figures 1–3.
V12-AFP_500.note: Five-year OS at final AFP <100 / 100–499 / ≥500: 72.7% / 70.4% / 56.1%; recurrence: 13.1% / 18.7% / 24.2%. Final AFP ≥500: adjusted mortality HR 1.50 (95% CI 1.07–2.10), recurrence HR 1.88 (1.13–3.14). Historical recipient-only study, not a comparison of transplant versus no transplant. Many had only one AFP. In the ≥500 subgroup, 40.4% were ≥1000; small subgroups cannot establish equivalence. Recurrence estimates censor competing death. Full PDF saved privately; TMC: https://libkey.io/libraries/480/10.1002/lt.26392

V12-AFP_SLOPE.title: Alpha-Fetoprotein Slope >7.5 ng/mL per Month Predicts Microvascular Invasion and Tumor Recurrence After Liver Transplantation for Hepatocellular Carcinoma.

V12-AFP_SLOPE.note: AFP slope >7.5 ng/mL/month: adjusted recurrence HR 3.0 (1.1–8.1), microvascular invasion OR 6.8 (1.6–28.7). Five-year recurrence-free probability 69.8% versus 87.4%; survival without recurrence 59.5% versus 75.3%. These are different endpoints, neither pair should be labeled overall survival. Small, data-selected cutoff group; no prospective hold/release validation. The long-term fitted slope cannot be inferred reliably from two closely spaced noisy results. Death was censored for recurrence-free probability. Full PDF saved privately; TMC: https://libkey.io/libraries/480/10.1097/TP.0000000000002094

V12-AFP_NYCA.title: Dynamic α-Fetoprotein Response and Outcomes After Liver Transplant for Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
V12-AFP_NYCA.locator: Main PDF pp 1–8; Table 1, Figures 1–3. Trailing commentary is not a separate reviewed study.
V12-AFP_NYCA.note: Five-year competing-risk cumulative recurrence: 9.5%, 20.5%, 40.5% for low/intermediate/high NYCA categories. Discrimination C statistic 0.66. These are composite-score categories, not isolated AFP ranges. Recipient selection, exclusion of early deaths, no waitlist dropout or transplant-benefit comparison. Maximum-to-final AFP can miss a rebound below the original peak. Extreme-AFP response subgroup was tiny. Full PDF saved privately; TMC: https://libkey.io/libraries/480/10.1001/jamasurg.2021.0954

V12-AFP_OCCULT.title: Management and Prognosis of HCC Patients With Elevated Tumor Markers but no Imaging Recurrence After Radiofrequency Ablation.
V12-AFP_OCCULT.locator: All nine main-PDF pages; methods, Tables 2–4, Figures 1–3. External Tables S1/S2 not supplied.
V12-AFP_OCCULT.note: Recurrence was subsequently identified in 886 episodes; median detection interval 89 days. Local curative treatment 83.5% versus 78.8% and post-recurrence OS 3.55 versus 3.31 years for detection ≤180 versus >180 days; differences were not statistically significant. RFA-specific, repeated episodes and competing losses; no LT cohort or tested optimal recall interval. Routine imaging is described as every four months in methods versus quarterly in abstract. Case-level AFP discrepancy between Figure 3 and Table 4 is not used. Full PDF saved privately; TMC: https://libkey.io/libraries/480/10.1002/cam4.71812

V12-SHARP.title: Sorafenib in Advanced Hepatocellular Carcinoma
V12-SHARP.locator: NEJM main PDF pp 1–13, especially efficacy and safety Tables 2–3.
V12-SHARP.note: Median OS 10.7 versus 7.9 months; HR 0.69 (0.55–0.87). Radiologic time to progression 5.5 versus 2.8 months, HR 0.58; this is not PFS. ORR 2% versus 1%, no complete responses. Historical placebo comparison, not a comparison with current ICI combinations. Grade 3 diarrhea and hand–foot reaction each 8%; dose interruptions/reductions frequent. Little evidence for decompensated cirrhosis. Full PDF saved privately; TMC: https://libkey.io/libraries/480/10.1056/NEJMoa0708857

V12-ASCO_BTC.title: Treatment of Advanced Biliary Tract Cancer: ASCO Living Guideline, Version 2026.1.0.
V12-ASCO_BTC.locator: All 56 pages; recommendations Table 1 pp 40–42; Figure 1 p 34 visually inspected. Separate data supplement not reviewed.
V12-ASCO_BTC.note: Broad tissue DNA/RNA profiling, MMR and HER2 testing at diagnosis. For eligible MSS/pMMR disease: GemCis plus durvalumab or pembrolizumab (high-quality/strong); GemCis without ICI if unsuitable (conditional). After progression without an actionable target: FOLFOX plus active symptom control or active symptom control alone (conditional). For oxaliplatin-ineligible patients, irinotecan/nal-IRI-based options have low-quality conditional support, not equal default status. Rare targets often rely on small basket cohorts. Accepted-manuscript tables/narrative contain inconsistent estimates; primary trial results govern this update. Full PDF saved privately; TMC: https://libkey.io/libraries/480/10.1200/JCO-26-02462

V12-NALIRICC.title: Nanoliposomal irinotecan and fluorouracil plus leucovorin versus fluorouracil plus leucovorin in patients with cholangiocarcinoma and gallbladder carcinoma previously treated with gemcitabine-based therapies (AIO NALIRICC): a multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 2 trial
V12-NALIRICC.locator: Main PDF pp 1–11; Figure 2 and Tables 1–3.
V12-NALIRICC.note: PFS 2.6 versus 2.3 months, HR 0.87 (0.56–1.35); OS 6.9 versus 8.2 months, HR 1.08 (0.68–1.72). ORR 14% versus 4% did not translate into PFS/OS benefit. Grade ≥3 events 71% versus 50%; treatment-related serious events 33% versus 2%. Small phase II trial; subsequent therapy differed (more control patients received later therapy). This does not erase the negative primary PFS result. Contrasts with positive NIFTY; population and treatment differences do not resolve the inconsistency. Full PDF saved privately; TMC: https://libkey.io/libraries/480/10.1016/S2468-1253(24)00119-5

V12-MOUNTAINEER.title: Tucatinib plus trastuzumab for chemotherapy-refractory, HER2 + , RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer (MOUNTAINEER): final analysis.
V12-MOUNTAINEER.locator: All 12 main-PDF pages; methods, efficacy Table 2, safety Table 4 and biomarker figures.
V12-MOUNTAINEER.note: Tucatinib plus trastuzumab: confirmed ORR 39.3% (28.8–50.5), median response duration 15.2 months, PFS 8.1 months, OS 23.9 months. Grade 3 and 4 events 33.7% and 7.0%; 5.8% discontinued for adverse events. No randomized combination comparator or proven best sequence after other HER2 drugs. Do not rank its median OS against unrelated later-line trials. Exploratory HER2 copy-number thresholds are not mandatory selection cutoffs. Full PDF saved privately; TMC: https://libkey.io/libraries/480/10.1038/s41467-025-67824-z

V12-SUNLIGHT.title: Trifluridine-Tipiracil and Bevacizumab in Refractory Metastatic Colorectal Cancer.
V12-SUNLIGHT.locator: All 11 main-PDF pages; Figures 1–2 and Tables 1–2.
V12-SUNLIGHT.note: OS 10.8 versus 7.5 months, HR 0.61 (0.49–0.77); PFS 5.6 versus 2.4 months, HR 0.44. ORR 6.1% versus 1.2%. Grade ≥3 events 72.4% versus 69.5%; neutropenia 43.1% versus 32.1%. Open-label; no head-to-head comparison with fruquintinib/regorafenib. Low response rate and an advanced refractory population: not a preferred curative conversion regimen or LT trial. Full PDF saved privately; TMC: https://libkey.io/libraries/480/10.1056/NEJMoa2214963

V12-FRESCO2.title: Fruquintinib versus placebo in patients with refractory metastatic colorectal cancer (FRESCO-2): an international, multicentre, randomised, double-blind, phase 3 study.
V12-FRESCO2.locator: All 13 main-PDF pages; Figures 2–3 and Tables 1–3.
V12-FRESCO2.note: Fruquintinib versus placebo plus supportive care: OS 7.4 versus 4.8 months, HR 0.66 (0.55–0.80); PFS 3.7 versus 1.8, HR 0.32. Seven partial responses among 461; no complete response. Grade ≥3 events 63% versus 50%. Very late-line population, no direct comparison with SUNLIGHT. Grade ≥3 hypertension 14%, asthenia 8%, hand–foot syndrome 6%; one treatment-related intestinal-perforation death. Full PDF saved privately; TMC: https://libkey.io/libraries/480/10.1016/S0140-6736(23)00772-9

V12-CASSANDRA.title: Preoperative mFOLFIRINOX versus PAXG for stage I–III resectable and borderline resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PACT-21 CASSANDRA): results of the first randomisation analysis of a randomised, open-label, 2 × 2 factorial phase 3 trial
V12-CASSANDRA.locator: All 12 main-PDF pages; endpoint definition, Figure 3 and Tables 1–3.
V12-CASSANDRA.note: Median event-free survival 16.0 versus 10.2 months, HR 0.63 (0.47–0.84). EFS included confirmed CA19-9 rises and unresectability, not just progression/death. Resection 75% versus 67% (not significant); R0 rates similar. Grade ≥3 toxicity 66% versus 61%. OS immature; no established OS superiority. Open-label, high-volume Italian centers, all White population, age cap. Converted phase II to III after 86% enrollment; no independent monitoring committee. Thirty-three EFS events were marker-only. Do not relabel EFS as OS or PFS. Full PDF saved privately; TMC: https://libkey.io/libraries/480/10.1016/S0140-6736(25)01685-X

V12-NAPOLI1.title: Nanoliposomal irinotecan with fluorouracil and folinic acid in metastatic pancreatic cancer after previous gemcitabine-based therapy (NAPOLI-1): a global, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial.
V12-NAPOLI1.locator: All 13 main-PDF pages; Figures 1–3 and Tables 1–3.
V12-NAPOLI1.note: nal-IRI plus 5-FU/LV: OS 6.1 versus 4.2 months, HR 0.67 (0.49–0.92); PFS 3.1 versus 1.5, HR 0.56. ORR 16% versus 1%. nal-IRI monotherapy did not improve OS (HR 0.99). Grade 3–4 neutropenia 27%, diarrhea 13%. Small prior-irinotecan subgroup, different 5-FU schedules, selected organ function. No validated immediate reuse after FOLFIRINOX/NALIRIFOX. One combination treatment-related septic-shock death. Full PDF saved privately; TMC: https://libkey.io/libraries/480/10.1016/S0140-6736(15)00986-1

V12-MIXED_PRIMARY.title: Multicenter retrospective analysis of systemic chemotherapy for unresectable combined hepatocellular and cholangiocarcinoma.
V12-MIXED_PRIMARY.locator: All nine main-PDF pages; Table 2 and Figure 3 p 5 visually inspected; Table 3 p 6.
V12-MIXED_PRIMARY.note: Overall OS 8.9 months, PFS 2.8 months, ORR 5.6%. Pooled platinum regimens had longer observed OS than sorafenib; adjusted sorafenib-versus-platinum mortality HR 15.83 (2.25–111.43). All seven sorafenib exposures including later line had progression. Tiny nonrandomized groups, major confounding and very wide CI. Abstract and body reverse individual GemCis/5-FU-cisplatin median ordering; do not present those medians as settled. Old pathology classification; no modern ICI comparison. Full PDF saved privately; TMC: https://libkey.io/libraries/480/10.1111/cas.13656

LRT-33230652.title: Evaluation of Medium-Term Efficacy of Y90 Radiation Segmentectomy vs Percutaneous Microwave Ablation in Patients with Solitary Surgically Unresectable < 4 cm Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Propensity Score Matched Study.
LRT-33230652.locator: Cardiovasc Intervent Radiol. 2021. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-33230652.note: Retrospective, propensity matched. Solitary treatment-naïve HCC ≤4 cm; 68 patients, 24 matched pairs. RS versus MWA. Mean target-tumor PFS 57.8 versus 38.6 months (p=0.005); mean OS 59.0 versus 44.3 months (p=0.203). Small matched cohorts; RS often selected for anatomy unsuitable for MWA. These are mean survival times, not medians. No proven OS superiority or equivalence. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-33230652.author: Arndt L

LRT-42434250.title: A retrospective study on the outcomes of yttrium-90 radiation segmentectomy with resin microspheres compared to microwave ablation for early primary hepatocellular carcinoma.
LRT-42434250.locator: J Gastrointest Oncol. 2026. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-42434250.note: Retrospective cohort. Solitary AJCC stage I HCC ≤4 cm; resin RS 20 versus MWA 40. RS tumors were larger. Main-text CR 85% versus 82.5%; adjusted PFS HR 0.56 (95% CI 0.20–1.51), OS HR 1.38 (0.30–6.34). No significant PFS/OS difference. Anatomy determined treatment; deaths within 1 month excluded. Abstract CR differs from main text; main-text denominator used. No equivalence conclusion. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-42434250.author: Abdalla O

LRT-27930089.title: Radiation Segmentectomy versus TACE Combined with Microwave Ablation for Unresectable Solitary Hepatocellular Carcinoma Up to 3 cm: A Propensity Score Matching Study.
LRT-27930089.locator: Radiology. 2017. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-27930089.note: Retrospective, propensity matched. Solitary HCC ≤3 cm; RS 41 versus TACE plus MWA 80 before matching. After matching: no significant difference in CR (p=0.94), time to progression (p=0.83), or OS (p>0.99). Comparator is TACE plus MWA, not MWA alone. Selection bias and limited power; nonsignificance does not establish equivalence. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-27930089.author: Biederman DM

LRT-36100064.title: Transarterial Radioembolization versus Transarterial Chemoembolization Plus Percutaneous Ablation for Unresectable, Solitary Hepatocellular Carcinoma of ≥3 cm: A Propensity Score-Matched Study.
LRT-36100064.locator: J Vasc Interv Radiol. 2022. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-36100064.note: Retrospective, propensity matched. Solitary unresectable HCC ≥3 cm; TARE versus DEB-TACE plus ablation; 19 matched pairs. DCR 94.7% versus 100%; locoregional sessions 1.3 versus 1.9 (p=0.02). No significant survival, PFS or transplant-rate difference. Combined comparator; small selected cohorts. Results do not show that TARE is superior to ablation alone. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-36100064.author: Yu Q

LRT-42379392.title: Radiation Segmentectomy versus Combined Chemoembolization plus Microwave Ablation: Histopathologic Tumor Necrosis in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Measuring up to 5 cm.
LRT-42379392.locator: J Vasc Interv Radiol. 2026. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-42379392.note: Retrospective explant study. 53 transplanted patients; RS 28 versus TACE-MWA 25; 40 tumors per group, HCC ≤5 cm. Mean pathologic tumor necrosis 83.6% versus 79.0% (p=0.484); treatment modality was not independently associated with complete necrosis. Transplanted patients only; cannot assess waitlist dropout. Complete-necrosis percentages have inconsistent denominators in Table 2 and are omitted. Most RS doses preceded current high-dose practice. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-42379392.author: Yu Q

LRT-35346857.title: Radiation Segmentectomy for the Treatment of Solitary Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Outcomes Compared with Those of Surgical Resection.
LRT-35346857.locator: J Vasc Interv Radiol. 2022. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-35346857.note: Retrospective multisite cohort. Solitary HCC ≤8 cm; RS 57 versus resection 66. Target progression 5% versus 8%; adjusted overall-progression HR 1.16 (95% CI 0.51–2.63). Median OS not reached in either group. Propensity distributions were too dissimilar to match. Different surgical candidacy and liver function prevent a claim of equivalence to resection. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-35346857.author: De la Garza-Ramos C

LRT-19552767.title: A comparative analysis of transarterial downstaging for hepatocellular carcinoma: chemoembolization versus radioembolization.
LRT-19552767.locator: Am J Transplant. 2009. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-19552767.note: Retrospective comparison. UNOS T3 HCC; 43 TARE versus 43 TACE patients. Downstaging to T2: Y90 25/43 (58%) versus TACE 11/35 (31%), p=0.023. The 61% versus 37% figures describe partial response. Retrospective. Eight TACE patients lacked follow-up imaging and were excluded from response analyses. Downstaging measured the whole lesion, including necrotic tissue; this is not the current viable-tumor method. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-19552767.author: Lewandowski RJ

LRT-34358718.title: National Trends and Waitlist Outcomes of Locoregional Therapy Among Liver Transplant Candidates With Hepatocellular Carcinoma in the United States.
LRT-34358718.locator: Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol. 2022. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-34358718.note: National observational cohort. 31,609 US HCC transplant candidates, 2003–2018; 24,145 received LRT. IPTW-adjusted dropout sHR versus TACE: radioembolization 0.85 (95% CI 0.81–0.89); thermal ablation 0.95 (0.91–0.99). Observational first-treatment comparison, with later treatments allowed. Center, era and patient selection remain confounders. Registry cohorts overlap with later studies. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-34358718.author: Kwong AJ

LRT-41056563.title: Evolving trends and comparative outcomes of bridging transarterial locoregional therapy in liver transplant candidates with hepatocellular carcinoma.
LRT-41056563.locator: Liver Transpl. 2026. Available main text checked for the stated results.
LRT-41056563.note: National observational cohort. 8,367 OPTN candidates, 2016–2024; sole modality TARE 2,895 versus TACE 5,472. Death/too-sick dropout sHR 0.83 (95% CI 0.74–0.93); complete-necrosis aOR 2.24 (1.88–2.67). No significant adjusted OS, post-LT OS or recurrence difference. Switching/mixed LRT and LDLT excluded; overlaps Kim registry population. Final issue 2026, online 2025. Available main text checked for the stated results.
LRT-41056563.author: Fakhoury B

LRT-41580092.title: Yttrium-90 radioembolization is associated with a lower risk of liver transplant waitlist dropout than chemoembolization in hepatocellular carcinoma.
LRT-41580092.locator: J Hepatol. 2026. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-41580092.note: National observational cohort, IPTW. 5,677 HCC-exception candidates, 2019–2024; first-line TARE versus TACE. Weighted cause-specific dropout HR 0.78 (95% CI 0.69–0.89); 2-year dropout 14.2% versus 19.0%. One LRT only: 80.6% versus 57.8%. Observational registry association; both-modality recipients excluded from the primary analysis. Treatment details and selection remain incompletely measured. No proven post-transplant survival advantage. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-41580092.author: Kim NG

LRT-39808828.title: Downstaging of hepatocellular carcinoma before liver transplantation: Results from a national multicenter prospective cohort study.
LRT-39808828.locator: Hepatology. 2025. Available main text checked for the stated results.
LRT-39808828.note: Prospective multicenter cohort. MERITS-LT: 326 within UNOS-DS and 190 all-comers beyond UNOS-DS; 2015–2023. In the all-comers subgroup, 2-year successful downstaging was 74% with initial Y90 versus 65% with TACE (p<0.001). Treatment was not randomized; subgroup finding does not expand allocation criteria. Overlaps earlier MERITS-LT enrollment. Earlier within-UNOS-DS study found no significant modality difference. Available main text checked for the stated results.
LRT-39808828.author: Xu E

LRT-28668402.title: Comparative study of post-transplant outcomes in hepatocellular carcinoma patients treated with chemoembolization or radioembolization.
LRT-28668402.locator: Eur J Radiol. 2017. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-28668402.note: Retrospective recipient cohort. 172 transplanted patients: Y90 93 versus TACE 79. Post-LT recurrence 9% versus 8%; RFS and OS did not differ significantly. Only recipients were analyzed. This cannot establish equivalent bridging success or compare dropout before transplantation. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-28668402.author: Gabr A

LRT-35619164.title: Bridging treatment prior to liver transplantation for hepatocellular carcinoma: radioembolization or transarterial chemoembolization?
LRT-35619164.locator: Eur J Med Res. 2022. Available main text checked for the stated results.
LRT-35619164.note: Retrospective recipient cohort. 131 recipients: Y90 44 versus TACE 87. Within Milan initially: 20.5% versus 65.5%. Post-LT recurrence 23% versus 11% (p=0.1224); no significant survival difference. Major baseline imbalance; pre-LT dropouts (6 Y90, 8 TACE) excluded. Recipient outcomes do not answer the waitlist-dropout question. Available main text checked for the stated results.
LRT-35619164.author: Benkö T

LRT-28799575.title: Comparison of outcomes between SBRT, yttrium-90 radioembolization, transarterial chemoembolization, and radiofrequency ablation as bridge to transplant for hepatocellular carcinoma.
LRT-28799575.locator: Adv Radiat Oncol. 2016. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-28799575.note: Retrospective recipient cohort. 60 recipients; 79 treatments across SBRT, TACE, RFA and Y90; only 9 Y90 and 9 RFA treatments. Complete pathologic response was reported in 75% after Y90 and 60% after RFA among evaluable explants. Very small, unequal evaluable groups, mixed treatments and recipient selection; illustrative pathology results, not a modality ranking or dropout comparison. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-28799575.author: Mohamed M

LRT-27284477.title: Conformal external beam radiation or selective internal radiation therapy-a comparison of treatment outcomes for hepatocellular carcinoma.
LRT-27284477.locator: J Gastrointest Oncol. 2016. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-27284477.note: Retrospective registry analysis. SEER 2004–2011; 189 unresectable HCC patients, SIRT 77 versus coded SBRT 112. Adjusted OS HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.49–1.07) for SIRT versus SBRT; no significant difference. Older registry radiation coding and missing liver-function/dosimetry details limit applicability to modern RS versus SBRT. No equivalence conclusion. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-27284477.author: Oladeru OT

LRT-25443863.title: Pilot randomized trial of selective internal radiation therapy vs. chemoembolization in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma.
LRT-25443863.locator: Liver Int. 2015. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-25443863.note: Randomized pilot (SIRTACE). 28 unresectable HCC patients: single-session SIRT 13 versus repeated TACE 15. DCR 76.9% versus 73.3%; no significant difference in 12-week health-related quality of life. Safety/QoL pilot, not powered for survival or transplant endpoints. Complements, rather than confirms, PREMIERE and TRACE. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-25443863.author: Kolligs FT

LRT-25373796.title: Randomized comparison of selective internal radiotherapy (SIRT) versus drug-eluting bead transarterial chemoembolization (DEB-TACE) for the treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma.
LRT-25373796.locator: Cardiovasc Intervent Radiol. 2015. Abstract verified; full-text review is incomplete.
LRT-25373796.note: Randomized pilot. 24 predominantly BCLC-B HCC patients: SIRT versus DEB-TACE, 12 per arm. Median PFS 180 versus 216 days; OS 592 versus 788 days; neither difference significant. Four liver-failure deaths occurred after SIRT. Small trial with older delivery/dosimetry; no class-wide Y90 survival advantage. Abstract verified; full-text review is incomplete.
LRT-25373796.author: Pitton MB

LRT-33687130.title: Randomized controlled study to examine the efficacy of hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy with cisplatin before radiofrequency ablation for hepatocellular carcinoma.
LRT-33687130.locator: Hepatol Res. 2021. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-33687130.note: Randomized study. 70 early HCC patients: cisplatin HAIC before RFA versus RFA alone, 35 per arm. 3-year RFS 54.3% versus 34.3%; HR 0.597 (95% CI 0.320–1.091), p=0.094. Primary RFS endpoint was not significant. A secondary distant-intrahepatic recurrence signal does not establish routine HAIC addition or HAIC as a replacement for ablation. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-33687130.author: Oyama A

LRT-35993224.title: Hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy and sequential ablation treatment in large hepatocellular carcinoma.
LRT-35993224.locator: Int J Hyperthermia. 2022. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-35993224.note: Retrospective, IPTW. 228 HCC patients with tumors >5 cm: HAIC followed by ablation 93 versus HAIC alone 135. Reported 2-year OS: 74.3% versus 27.7%. IPTW and 6-month landmark analyses favored HAIC followed by ablation. Selected HAIC responders; substantial selection bias. Reported survival medians conflict with Results/Figure 2 and are omitted. Tests adding ablation after HAIC, not replacing ablation with HAIC. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-35993224.author: You H

LRT-29631810.title: Sorafenib plus low-dose cisplatin and fluorouracil hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy versus sorafenib alone in patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (SILIUS): a randomised, open label, phase 3 trial.
LRT-29631810.locator: Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol. 2018. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-29631810.note: Randomized phase III (SILIUS). 206 advanced HCC patients; low-dose cisplatin/5-FU HAIC plus sorafenib versus sorafenib. Median OS 11.8 versus 11.5 months; HR 1.009 (95% CI 0.743–1.371), p=0.955. Negative OS trial. Regimen differs from FOLFOX-HAIC trials; increased hematologic toxicity. Do not generalize a benefit across all HAIC regimens. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-29631810.author: Kudo M

LRT-40709764.title: Hepatic Artery Infusion Chemotherapy Compared to Transarterial Radioembolization For Unresectable Colorectal Liver Metastases.
LRT-40709764.locator: Ann Surg. 2025. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-40709764.note: Retrospective multicenter, propensity matched. 708 HAI versus 481 TARE patients; matched within prior systemic-therapy lines. TARE-versus-HAI mortality HR: 1 prior line 1.46 (95% CI 1.02–2.08); 2 lines 1.96 (1.32–2.89); 3–4 lines 0.88 (0.57–1.35). HAI came from one high-volume center, TARE from five others. More subsequent systemic therapy/resection after HAI; treatment and center effects cannot be separated. Not a comparison with ablation. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-40709764.author: Saadat LV

LRT-29181682.title: Effectiveness of Hepatic Artery Infusion (HAI) Versus Selective Internal Radiation Therapy (Y90) for Pretreated Isolated Unresectable Colorectal Liver Metastases (IU-CRCLM).
LRT-29181682.locator: Ann Surg Oncol. 2018. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-29181682.note: Retrospective comparison. 97 pretreated liver-only CRLM patients: HAI 48 versus Y90 49, with modern systemic therapy. Median OS from isolated unresectable diagnosis: 31.2 versus 16.3 months (p<0.001). From initial stage IV diagnosis: 34.4 versus 32.0 months (p=0.291). Retrospective, 97 patients. Survival time origin changes the apparent comparison; treatment timing, subsequent therapy and selection limit causal interpretation. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-29181682.author: Dhir M

LRT-11843249.title: Randomised trial of SIR-Spheres plus chemotherapy vs. chemotherapy alone for treating patients with liver metastases from primary large bowel cancer.
LRT-11843249.locator: Ann Oncol. 2001. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-11843249.note: Randomized phase III. 74 patients with bilobar unresectable CRLM: Y90 plus regional FUDR versus regional FUDR alone. Tumor-volume response 50% versus 24% (p=0.03); liver progression was delayed. Tests adding Y90 to HAI, not Y90 versus HAI alone. Older chemotherapy era; no established overall-survival benefit. Not evidence against ablation of small lesions. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-11843249.author: Gray B

LRT-31177151.title: Comparison of Response and Outcomes of Drug-eluting Bead Chemoembolization (DEB-TACE) Versus Radioembolization (TARE) for Patients With Colorectal Cancer Liver Metastases.
LRT-31177151.locator: Anticancer Res. 2019. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-31177151.note: Retrospective, propensity matched. 202 CRLM patients; 44 matched pairs, DEB-TACE versus TARE. Adjusted OS association for DEB-TACE: HR 0.94 (95% CI 0.54–1.65), p=0.83; toxicity trend 27% versus 9.1%, p=0.057. No significant survival difference; baseline burden and extrahepatic disease varied. Not an equivalence trial. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-31177151.author: Mokkarala M

LRT-41118066.title: Treatment Intensification with Hepatic Arterial Infusion Chemotherapy in Patients with Liver-Only Colorectal Metastases Still Unresectable After Systemic Induction Chemotherapy: Exploratory Findings From a Prematurely Closed Multicenter Randomized Phase II Study: SULTAN UCGI 30/PRODIGE 53 (NCT03164655).
LRT-41118066.locator: Ann Surg Oncol. 2026. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-41118066.note: Prematurely closed randomized phase II (SULTAN). Persistently unresectable liver-only CRLM after systemic induction; 11 HAI-oxaliplatin plus systemic versus 9 systemic alone randomized. Conversion to resection/ablation 7/11 (64%) versus 2/9 (22%), p=0.09; PFS 12.6 versus 4.37 months. Very small, early-closed trial; conversion endpoint not significant. Supports further study, not a confirmed conversion advantage or direct comparison against ablation. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-41118066.author: Boilève A

LRT-39644535.title: Safety and efficacy of adjuvant FOLFOX/FOLFIRI with versus without hepatic arterial infusion of floxuridine in patients following colorectal cancer liver metastasectomy (HARVEST trial): A randomized controlled trial.
LRT-39644535.locator: Eur J Cancer. 2025. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-39644535.note: Prematurely stopped randomized trial (HARVEST). 92 randomized after CRLM surgery; modified ITT 77, HAI-FUDR plus systemic 38 versus systemic 39. 3-year RFS 31.4% versus 34.4%, p=0.28. Stopped for FUDR supply shortage; primary endpoint negative. Exploratory early-RFS/subgroup signals do not establish routine postoperative HAI. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-39644535.author: Wang DS

LRT-42018958.title: Postoperative Hepatic Arterial Infusion With Oxaliplatin After Surgery of Four or More Colorectal Liver Metastases: A Randomized Phase II Trial.
LRT-42018958.locator: J Clin Oncol. 2026. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-42018958.note: Randomized phase II. 99 patients after resection/ablation of ≥4 CRLM: HAI-oxaliplatin 50 versus IV oxaliplatin 49, both with IV LV5FU2. Hepatic RFS 25 versus 12 months, HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.40–0.99); OS HR 0.61 (0.33–1.12), not significant. Grade 3–4 AEs 58% versus 32%. Selected adjuvant setting after complete local treatment of ≥4 CRLM. Phase II design amended before database lock; early closure and immature OS limit certainty. Oxaliplatin infusion is not FUDR pump therapy. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-42018958.author: Gelli M

LRT-42829779.title: Microwave ablation versus stereotactic body radiotherapy for oligometastatic colorectal liver metastases (LAVA-CRLM): a prospective, randomised, phase II trial.
LRT-42829779.locator: Lancet Reg Health Eur. 2026. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-42829779.note: Randomized phase II (LAVA-CRLM). 1–3 CRLM, each ≤4 cm and suitable for both treatments; 100 randomized, 92 modified ITT. 1-year freedom from local progression: MWA 77.7% versus SBRT 83.0%; HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.43–1.74), p=0.70. Grade ≥2 toxicity 25% versus 3%. No demonstrated local-control difference; wide CI and postrandomization exclusions. No survival/noninferiority claim. Grade ≥3 toxicity occurred only after MWA, including one treatment-related death. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-42829779.author: Risumlund SL

LRT-33868997.title: Survival Comparisons of Hepatic Arterial Infusion Chemotherapy With mFOLFOX and Transarterial Chemoembolization in Patients With Unresectable Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma.
LRT-33868997.locator: Front Oncol. 2021. Available main text checked for the stated results.
LRT-33868997.note: Retrospective cohort. 126 unresectable iCCA patients; mFOLFOX-HAIC versus TACE. 1-year OS 60.2% versus 42.9%; 2-year OS 38.7% versus 29.4% (OS comparison p=0.028). PFS did not differ significantly. Nonrandomized, regional catheter regimen. Does not establish pump-FUDR superiority or replace contemporary systemic therapy. Available main text checked for the stated results.
LRT-33868997.author: Cai Z

LRT-40216615.title: Hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy versus transarterial chemoembolization in patients with unresectable intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
LRT-40216615.locator: Eur Radiol. 2025. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-40216615.note: Retrospective multicenter cohort. 181 patients: HAIC 24, conventional TACE 73, DEB-TACE 84. HAIC versus conventional TACE median OS 10.3 versus 5.1 months (p=0.0042); no significant HAIC-versus-DEB-TACE difference reported. Very small HAIC cohort; treatment selection and TACE formulation matter. Do not generalize the comparison to all arterial therapy. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-40216615.author: Zhang Y

LRT-35544131.title: Comparison of Hepatic Arterial Infusion Pump Chemotherapy vs Resection for Patients With Multifocal Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma.
LRT-35544131.locator: JAMA Surg. 2022. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-35544131.note: Retrospective comparison. 319 multifocal iCCA patients: unresectable HAIP-FUDR 141 versus resection 178 across different centers/eras. Median OS 20.3 versus 18.9 months; adjusted HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.55–1.03), p=0.07. HAIP patients had substantially more bilobar/multifocal disease. Not an equivalence trial or reason to deny resection to an otherwise suitable patient; does not distinguish all satellites from metastases. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-35544131.author: Franssen S

LRT-37814188.title: Gemcitabine with Cisplatin Versus Hepatic Arterial Infusion Pump Chemotherapy for Liver-Confined Unresectable Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma.
LRT-37814188.locator: Ann Surg Oncol. 2024. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-37814188.note: Retrospective cross-center cohort. 268 liver-confined unresectable iCCA patients: HAIP ± systemic 192 versus gemcitabine/cisplatin 76. Median OS 27.7 versus 11.8 months; approximately one third of HAIP patients alive at 3 years. Nonrandomized center, era and treatment-line differences; 71.9% of HAIP patients also received systemic treatment. Comparator predates current chemoimmunotherapy; not HAI versus Y90 or ablation. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-37814188.author: Franssen S

LRT-30191056.title: Chemoembolization versus radioembolization for the treatment of unresectable intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma in a single institution image-based efficacy and comparative toxicity.
LRT-30191056.locator: Hepat Oncol. 2017. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-30191056.note: Retrospective cohort. 40 unresectable iCCA patients: Y90 25 versus chemoembolization 15. Table 3 disease control: Y90 12/25 (48%) versus chemoembolization 7/15 (47%); no significant difference. Survival was not assessed. Small retrospective cohort. Abstract and body percentages conflict; counts from Table 3 are used. Missing response status and treatment crossover limit comparison. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-30191056.author: Akinwande O

LRT-31517072.title: Stereotactic body radiation therapy is associated with improved overall survival compared to chemoradiation or radioembolization in the treatment of unresectable intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
LRT-31517072.locator: Clin Transl Radiat Oncol. 2019. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-31517072.note: Retrospective NCDB comparison. Main-text analysis: SBRT 27, chemoradiation 54, TARE 60; nonmetastatic node-negative unresected iCCA. Adjusted OS HR 0.42 (95% CI 0.21–0.84) for SBRT versus TARE. TARE tumors were larger/more often multifocal or vascular-invasive. Strong selection bias and abstract/main-text cohort-count discrepancy; not causal superiority or equivalent treatment eligibility. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-31517072.author: Sebastian NT

LRT-42433279.title: Biliary drainage plus hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy versus biliary drainage plus best supportive care for advanced perihilar cholangiocarcinoma in China: a prospective multicentre non-randomised controlled study.
LRT-42433279.locator: EClinicalMedicine. 2026. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-42433279.note: Prospective nonrandomized cohort. 127 advanced pCCA patients after biliary drainage: catheter HAIC 63 versus best supportive care 64; preserved reserve, no distant/N2 disease. Median OS 17.63 versus 6.10 months. Patient preference/clinical selection; no contemporary systemic-therapy comparator. Hypothesis-generating disease-control evidence, not established standard, cure, or a transplant-bridging protocol. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-42433279.author: Dai Y

LRT-29167951.title: Radioembolization Versus Bland Embolization for Hepatic Metastases from Small Intestinal Neuroendocrine Tumors: Short-Term Results of a Randomized Clinical Trial.
LRT-29167951.locator: World J Surg. 2018. Available main text checked for the stated results.
LRT-29167951.note: Randomized pilot. 11 small-intestinal NET patients: Y90 6 versus bland embolization 5. 3-month RECIST response 0/6 versus 5/5 (p=0.0022); 6-month response 2/6 versus 4/5, not significant. Tiny study; response timing differs after radiation. No survival ranking and no extrapolation to all NET primaries. Available main text checked for the stated results.
LRT-29167951.author: Elf AK

LRT-32032719.title: Transarterial Chemoembolization vs Radioembolization for Neuroendocrine Liver Metastases: A Multi-Institutional Analysis.
LRT-32032719.locator: J Am Coll Surg. 2020. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-32032719.note: Retrospective two-center cohort. 248 NELM patients: TARE 51 versus TACE 197. Initial DCR 83% versus 96% (p<0.01); no significant OS or PFS difference. TARE was usually outpatient. Nonrandomized baseline and treatment-selection differences. Does not prove equivalence; treatment burden and delayed toxicity also matter. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-32032719.author: Egger ME

LRT-28677067.title: Intra-arterial therapy of neuroendocrine tumour liver metastases: comparing conventional TACE, drug-eluting beads TACE and yttrium-90 radioembolisation as treatment options using a propensity score analysis model.
LRT-28677067.locator: Eur Radiol. 2017. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-28677067.note: Retrospective, propensity analysis. 192 GEP-NET patients: cTACE 122, DEB-TACE 26, Y90 44. Propensity-weighted median OS: cTACE versus Y90 34.0 versus 22.9 months (p=0.032); cTACE versus DEB-TACE 33.8 versus 23.4 months (p=0.04). Retrospective pairwise weighting across a long treatment era. These adjusted medians differ from the unadjusted three-group medians. Residual confounding prevents a definitive modality ranking. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-28677067.author: Do Minh D

LRT-33004146.title: Chronic Hepatotoxicity in Patients with Metastatic Neuroendocrine Tumor: Transarterial Chemoembolization versus Transarterial Radioembolization.
LRT-33004146.locator: J Vasc Interv Radiol. 2020. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-33004146.note: Retrospective survivor cohort. NELM patients surviving ≥1 year: TACE 63 versus TARE 28; chronic grade ≥3 hepatic toxicity beginning ≥6 months after treatment. Chronic hepatic toxicity: 22% versus 29%. Injury attributed solely to embolotherapy: 3% versus 14% (p=0.07), with more clinical decompensation after TARE. Retrospective survivor-selected cohort. Most TACE toxicities coincided with progression. This cannot estimate toxicity in all treated patients or establish equivalent safety. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-33004146.author: Currie BM

LRT-42006283.title: Yttrium-90 Radioembolization Versus Transarterial Embolization for Lung Carcinoid Hepatic Metastasis.
LRT-42006283.locator: JTO Clin Res Rep. 2026. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-42006283.note: Retrospective single-center cohort. 30 lung-carcinoid patients, 53 primary embolization procedures; Y90 versus bland TAE. Local progression-free survival 30.57 versus 13.9 months (p=0.01); OS 43.5 versus 40.6 months (p=0.49). Primary-specific, small retrospective study with repeated procedures and systemic-treatment confounding; not generalizable to all NELM. Full-text design and key outcomes checked, 4 November 2026.
LRT-42006283.author: Yuan G

LRT-32749512.title: Correlation of Y90-absorbed radiation dose to pathological necrosis in hepatocellular carcinoma: confirmatory multicenter analysis in 45 explants.
LRT-32749512.locator: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging. 2021;48:580–583. Table 1 p.581; Figure 3 p.582.
LRT-32749512.note: Retrospective multicenter surgical cohort: treatment-naive solitary HCC ≤8 cm, Child-Pugh A; glass-microsphere radiation segmentectomy followed by transplant (34) or resection (11). Complete pathologic necrosis 30/45 (67%); >400 Gy: 11/11 (100%). Only patients who reached surgery were assessed; the >400 Gy subgroup had 11 patients. Dose refers to the perfused tumor-bearing segment by MIRD, not tumor-only dose. No comparator, waitlist-dropout estimate or demonstrated survival advantage.
LRT-32749512.author: Gabr A
LRT-32749512.journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

old.text: Specify the treatment goal: bridging controls tumor while awaiting transplant; downstaging reduces tumor burden to transplant selection limits. Document anatomy, liver reserve, anticipated wait and the reason for the chosen treatment.

new.text: Specify the treatment goal: bridging controls tumor while awaiting transplant; downstaging reduces tumor burden to transplant selection limits. Document anatomy, liver reserve, anticipated wait and the reason for the chosen treatment. For radiation segmentectomy, document the treated volume and absorbed segment dose.

old.title: Continue or change liver-directed treatment
old.when: There is treatable liver disease, and liver reserve and anatomy permit another local treatment.
tasks: Continue the current downstaging approach if it is producing useful tumor control and remains safe. If response is inadequate, review a different modality with interventional radiology and radiation oncology.
Options include ablation, arterial treatment such as TACE or Y90, and radiation such as SBRT. Select by viable tumor location, prior treatment, normal-liver exposure and liver function.

If no suitable viable target remains, clarify the AFP rise and staging before repeating liver-directed treatment. If local treatment is unsuitable or ineffective, review systemic therapy, a trial or best supportive care.
Recheck imaging and AFP after treatment, then reassess transplant and MELD-exception criteria.

Ablation and selected Y90 radiation segmentectomy can both have curative intent. Choose by tumor size, location, liver reserve, achievable ablation margin or segmental dosimetry. Ablation has more randomized comparative evidence. Y90 versus ablation studies are mainly observational. Y90 is associated with less waitlist dropout than TACE in registry analyses, but no dedicated randomized comparison establishes a transplant or survival advantage.

If no suitable viable target remains, clarify the AFP rise and staging before repeating liver-directed treatment. If local treatment is unsuitable or ineffective, review systemic therapy, a trial or best supportive care.
Recheck imaging and AFP after treatment, then reassess transplant and MELD-exception criteria.

Ablation and selected Y90 radiation segmentectomy can both have curative intent. Choose by tumor size, location, liver reserve, achievable ablation margin or segmental dosimetry. Ablation has more randomized comparative evidence. Y90 versus ablation studies are mainly observational. Y90 is associated with less waitlist dropout than TACE in registry analyses, but no dedicated randomized comparison establishes a transplant or survival advantage.

For selected radiation segmentectomy, Gabr found complete necrosis in 30/45 surgical specimens (67%), including 11/11 after >400 Gy to the perfused segment. These recipient-only results support local tumor destruction; continue to assess transplant readiness using imaging, AFP, liver function and allocation criteria.
