{
  "15042359": {
    "kind": "rct",
    "limitations": [
      "Compliance with screening was only 58.2 percent",
      "The higher crude incidence in the screened arm points to over-diagnosis, which the authors acknowledge",
      "The authors estimate a lead time of about 0.5 years"
    ],
    "critique": [
      "Allocation was by cluster, with whole factories, schools and enterprises assigned together, but the analysis treated individuals as independent observations; an independent reanalysis calculated that the mortality difference would almost certainly have been non-significant had the clustering been accounted for",
      "384 of the 9,757 people allocated to screening were removed after randomisation because they refused, so the analysis is not intention to treat despite the paper's claim, and every exclusion is on the intervention side",
      "Only HCC deaths were counted and all-cause mortality was never reported, so neither harm from screening and the surgery it leads to nor misattribution of cause of death can be excluded, and the standard safeguard against disease-specific mortality bias is absent",
      "The screened arm's crude incidence was 37 percent higher than the control arm's, which is the signature of over-diagnosis, and the paper offers no analysis of how much of the mortality difference that could generate",
      "Survival comparisons between the arms are timed from diagnosis, which is lead-time biased by construction, and the authors' own estimated lead time of about half a year is of the same order as the survival differences reported",
      "The population is hepatitis B carriers and people with past hepatitis aged 35 to 59 in Shanghai, mostly without documented cirrhosis and screened with alpha-fetoprotein as a co-test, so it maps poorly onto a Western cirrhotic ultrasound surveillance cohort in whom alpha-fetoprotein is no longer recommended as a screening test",
      "Treatment of screen-detected cancers was resection in a pre-BCLC era with no transplantation or ablation pathway, so the mortality benefit depends on a treatment algorithm that no longer exists",
      "The paper's own figures disagree: the narrative gives the stage III split as 22 (25.6 percent) against 45 (62.9 percent) while the table gives 22 against 42 (62.7 percent), and resection in controls is 5 (7.5 percent) in the table against 7.8 percent in the text",
      "Compliance of 58.2 percent means that the measured effect is that of offering screening to a workplace population, and the paper presents no per-protocol or compliance-adjusted estimate alongside it"
    ],
    "n": "18,816 people aged 35 to 59 with serological evidence of hepatitis B infection or a history of chronic hepatitis, recruited from more than 300 factories, enterprises and schools in urban Shanghai between January 1993 and December 1995 and cluster-allocated to 6-monthly alpha-fetoprotein and ultrasound screening (9,757 allocated, 9,373 analysed) or no screening (9,443); cirrhosis was neither required nor excluded",
    "bottom_line": "The single randomised trial behind the recommendation for 6-monthly HCC surveillance, reporting a 37 percent reduction in HCC mortality with screening (83.2 against 131.5 per 100,000). Allocation was by cluster but the analysis treated individuals as independent, 384 people who refused were removed from the screening arm after allocation, and all-cause mortality was never reported.",
    "funding": "No funding statement; the trial predates registries and has no registration number"
  },
  "16495695": {
    "kind": "rct",
    "limitations": [
      "Post-randomisation exclusion occurred in 19 of 90 patients assigned to ablation, all of whom withdrew consent and chose resection; the authors state they do not think this affected the results",
      "Mean follow-up was only just beyond 2 years, and the authors state they do not expect a difference with longer follow-up",
      "The sample size was relatively small, and the authors argue a larger sample would not have changed the result because the curves were almost identical",
      "The authors concede that for ablation to work the first session must be followed by CT at 4 weeks and a further session of ablation or ethanol injection if viable tumour remains"
    ],
    "critique": [
      "The analysis labelled intention to treat is not one: the 90-patient ablation arm includes the 19 patients who actually underwent resection, so 21 percent of the experimental arm received the comparator operation, and the abstract instead quotes the post-randomisation-exclusion analysis of 71 against 90",
      "All 19 consent withdrawals went in the same direction, from ablation to surgery, which is the signature of unconcealed allocation; randomisation is described only as computer-generated numbers in a central registry with no concealment mechanism, no blinding and no independent outcome adjudication",
      "No hazard ratio, confidence interval or p value is printed anywhere for the primary survival comparison; survival was computed by the life-table method and compared by Mantel-Cox, and the result is reported only as the assertion that no difference was found",
      "The multivariable Cox model in Table 2 prints regression coefficients without their signs and no hazard ratios or confidence intervals, and reports serum albumin as the only predictor of survival (p = 0.0018) in a model of nine variables fitted to a cohort with roughly 50 deaths",
      "Four-year survival is the longest estimate reported although mean follow-up was 27.9 and 29.2 months, and no at-risk numbers appear under any of the ten survival curves, so the terminal estimates rest on an unstated handful of patients",
      "The morbidity comparison sets 50 of 90 resections against 3 of 71 ablations, mixing the two different analysis populations in one sentence, and 46 of the 50 surgical events are moderate-to-severe ascites (27) or jaundice beyond 30 days (19) counted as major complications with no validated grading system",
      "The ablation arm's harms were captured only as skin burns (3) and fever (8), with no systematic ascertainment of ascites, jaundice or liver dysfunction at all, which is why its complication count is 3; the two arms were not monitored for the same events",
      "Ablation as tested is a strategy rather than a procedure: complete necrosis was 62.0 percent after the first session and reached 91.5 percent only after repeat ablation or ethanol injection in 21 patients and chemoembolisation in 2, so 8.5 percent of the arm never achieved necrosis yet remained in its survival curve",
      "A single device was used (RF 2000 with a 3.5 cm LeVeen expandable electrode) with the endpoint of a hyperechoic cloud larger than the tumour on ultrasound and no margin requirement, which is not an adequate technique for tumours approaching 5 cm, and 34 of 71 ablated tumours measured 3.1 to 5 cm",
      "Diagnosis was imaging-based with an alpha-fetoprotein threshold: one resected specimen proved to be focal nodular hyperplasia and two patients had disseminated disease found at laparotomy, so at least 3 of 90 surgical patients did not have the disease under study and equivalent misclassification in the ablation arm could not be detected",
      "The stated sample size calculation specifies an alpha risk of 0.05 and a beta risk of 0.8, which is the power rather than the beta risk, and the trial was powered on 2-year recurrence rather than on survival, so the survival conclusion that the paper advertises was never the question the design could answer",
      "The 3 cm and 3.1 to 5 cm subgroup analyses involve 37 and 34 ablation patients and are reported as non-significant with no estimates, confidence intervals or interaction tests given",
      "The comparator is open surgery as practised in one Chinese centre in 1999 to 2004, with a right subcostal incision, routine Pringle manoeuvre in 10 and 5 minute cycles and a mean 19.7-day hospital stay against 9.2 days, so the length-of-stay and analgesia advantages do not transfer to a laparoscopic era",
      "The authors answer each of their three stated limitations by assuming the null they are defending, arguing in turn that the exclusions, the short follow-up and the small sample would not have changed a result whose curves were already superimposed"
    ],
    "n": "180 patients with a solitary HCC of 5 cm or less randomised at one Guangzhou centre between November 1999 and June 2004, drawn from 3,775 patients with HCC hospitalised there; 90 to percutaneous ablation (of whom only 71 received it) and 90 to resection",
    "bottom_line": "The first randomised comparison of percutaneous ablation with resection for a solitary HCC of 5 cm or less, reporting 4-year overall survival of 67.9 versus 64.0 percent and disease-free survival of 46.4 versus 51.6 percent with no significant difference. Nineteen of 90 patients assigned to ablation withdrew and had surgery instead, ablation as delivered needed repeat sessions to reach 91.5 percent necrosis from 62.0 percent after one treatment, and no hazard ratio or confidence interval for the primary comparison appears anywhere in the paper.",
    "funding": "Supported by a grant from the Sciences and Technology Committee of Guangdong Province, China, 2002; no conflict-of-interest statement appears in the article"
  },
  "18008357": {
    "kind": "cohort",
    "limitations": [
      "The comparison with surgery is historical, drawn from three surgical series, and the authors acknowledge the well-known limitations of historical comparison",
      "Fourteen of 232 eligible patients (6.0 percent) could not be treated because the tumour was poorly visible on ultrasound or lay next to bowel or main bile ducts",
      "Three of the treatment failures occurred next to a large vessel, which the authors attribute to heat loss in the ablation zone",
      "The authors state that a randomised trial of ablation against resection below 2 cm would need a very large sample and is probably not feasible",
      "The authors concede that the high overall recurrence rate shows it is the natural history of the cirrhotic liver, not the first treatment, that governs prognosis, and that all published survival curves reflect repeated multimodal treatment"
    ],
    "critique": [
      "The 68 percent 5-year survival in the abstract and conclusion is that of the 100 patients retrospectively judged operable; the whole cohort's figure of 55 percent appears only once in the Results and never in the abstract, so the number set against surgical series is a selected subgroup",
      "Operability was assigned by the authors from age 75 or under, alanine transferase under three times normal, bilirubin under 1.5 and absence of portal hypertension, with no surgeon assessing any patient, and operability was not an independent predictor of survival once adjusted (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.31 to 1.26, p = 0.192), so the subgroup that carries the headline does not survive multivariable analysis",
      "Three different complete-response figures appear in the same paper: 216 of 218 (97.2 percent) in the abstract, 214 of 218 (98.1 percent) complete radiological necrosis in the Results and 212 of 218 (97.2 percent) sustained complete local response; 216 of 218 is 99.1 percent, so the abstract's numerator and percentage do not correspond",
      "The classification boundary creates the result: enhancement within the ablation zone or up to 2.0 cm from its border is local recurrence, anything beyond 2.0 cm is a new lesion, which yields a 0.9 percent local recurrence rate in a cohort where 80 percent of patients recurred somewhere in the liver",
      "Disease-free survival of 26 percent at 3 years and 20 percent at 5 years is computed on 82 patients rather than 218, and the paper never states which 82 or why, while quoting confidence intervals as wide as 7 to 36 percent",
      "The 14 patients excluded for poor ultrasound visibility or a high-risk location are precisely the tumours in which ablation fails and resection is straightforward, so the local-control endpoint is measured on ground selected to favour the technique; the paper also states that 218 of 232 is 93.3 percent when it is 94.0 percent",
      "Technique was not standardised in any respect: five departments used at least four different electrode systems, including a 1.5 cm laterally deployed spiral, with power and exposure left to manufacturer recommendation and operator preference, and adequacy was judged by the extent of a hyperechoic cloud rather than by a measured margin on post-treatment imaging",
      "Pathological confirmation of the 97.2 percent local response consists of the explants of the 3 patients who were transplanted and censored at transplantation, so 215 of 218 local responses rest on contrast CT alone, with follow-up imaging only every 4 to 6 months",
      "Patients with any prospect of transplantation were excluded by design, so the cohort systematically omits the patients in whom the choice between ablation and resection carries the greatest consequence, and the authors justify this by Italian organ scarcity rather than by the clinical question",
      "The only significant multivariable predictor of survival is the appearance of new lesions during follow-up (HR 1.97, 1.13 to 3.5), a post-treatment event entered as a predictor of a survival time it partly determines, and alpha-fetoprotein could not be analysed at all because only 11 patients had raised values, so the model contains no measure of tumour biology",
      "Median follow-up was 31 months against 3- and 5-year endpoints in a cohort followed from 6 to 134 months, and no at-risk numbers appear under any survival curve",
      "The surgical mortality the paper contrasts with its own 0 percent is a literature mean of 5 percent spanning 0 to 15 percent across series from different decades and countries, while the Italian hepatitis C surveillance population here (83.9 percent HCV, mean age 68, 44 percent female, 21.5 percent over 75) is compared with Japanese surgical cohorts",
      "One of the four major complications is hyperbilirubinaemia lasting a month, and one is neoplastic seeding, so the 1.8 percent figure that anchors the safety argument contains a tumour implant from the procedure itself",
      "The paper concludes that ablation should be the treatment of choice even when resection is possible, a statement of superiority drawn from an uncontrolled cohort by authors who in the same Discussion declare the controlled test of it unfeasible"
    ],
    "n": "218 of 232 eligible patients with a single HCC of 2.0 cm or less and Child-Pugh A cirrhosis, treated by percutaneous radiofrequency ablation at 5 Italian departments between October 1995 and June 2006; 100 were retrospectively judged potentially operable",
    "bottom_line": "A multicentre cohort showing that radiofrequency ablation of a single HCC of 2 cm or less achieves sustained complete local response in 97.2 percent with no mortality and a 1.8 percent major complication rate. The 68 percent 5-year survival used to argue that ablation can replace resection belongs to a retrospectively defined operable subgroup of 100 patients, not to the cohort, whose 5-year survival was 55 percent with 80 percent recurrence and 20 percent disease-free survival; there is no control group and the authors argue the randomised trial that would settle it is not feasible.",
    "funding": "No funding statement appears; the authors declare no potential conflict of interest"
  },

  "24937669": {

It cannot establish equivalence, because it was powered for an implausible 20-point survival gain and stopped at 83 percent of its planned size, and nearly half its patients were early-stage with a median tumour under 3 cm.",
    "funding": "No funding source is identified in the article; the authors declare no conflict of interest"

  "25212123": {
    "kind": "meta-analysis",
    "limitations": [
      "The analysis pools observational and mostly retrospective data, which the authors state limits the ability to control for confounding",
      "Because most included studies did not adjust for known confounders, the authors were forced to use crude measures of association",
      "Four of the eleven studies scored 10 on the QUIPS tool and were rated high risk of bias",
      "The definition of clinical decompensation varied across studies, although all included jaundice and ascites",
      "The authors acknowledge that surgical practice has moved on since the included cohorts, naming laparoscopic resection, reduced clamping and portal vein embolisation, though they argue resection does not lower portal pressure",
      "The authors note that the reliability of observational methodology is hard to judge from published reports, which is why they restricted the search to full publications and excluded the grey literature"
    ],
    "critique": [
      "The search window opens in January 1996 because that is when the authors' own first paper on the question appeared, and four of the eleven included studies come from the authors' own group, so a meta-analysis described in its Discussion as validating the EASL and AASLD recommendations is conducted by the authors of those recommendations using their own data",
      "The decompensation subgroup estimate that drives the recommendation to measure the hepatic venous pressure gradient (pooled OR 14.59, 95% CI 2.81 to 80.06) rests on three studies of 29, 40 and 46 patients, two of them from the authors' unit, and the smallest of the three has perfect separation so its true odds ratio is unbounded",
      "The corresponding mortality subgroup estimate for gradient-based studies (OR 8.00, 95% CI 2.59 to 24.69) comes from the same group's 1996 and 1999 papers, so the claim that invasive measurement outperforms surrogates is a comparison between the authors' small prospective series and other groups' larger retrospective ones",
      "That comparison is made between subgroups of studies rather than within patients: no included study measured the gradient and the surrogate criteria in the same patients and compared their prognostic performance, so the conclusion that surrogates cannot exclude clinically significant portal hypertension is not something the pooled data can establish",
      "Only 2 of the 8 survival studies reported portal hypertension as an independent predictor on multivariable analysis, a fact placed in a supplementary table while the abstract and conclusions report the pooled crude odds ratio, so the headline estimate cannot distinguish the harm of operating from the natural history of more advanced cirrhosis",
      "Operative mortality did not differ by portal hypertension status in any study that reported it (11.1 versus 5.1 percent, 4.6 versus 1.1 percent, 0.5 versus 0 percent, all non-significant), so whatever the pooled survival difference represents, it is not perioperative death",
      "Patients with portal hypertension systematically received different operations: anatomical resection in 39 versus 68 percent in the largest study (p < 0.001), 12.1 versus 33.1 percent in another (p = 0.0003), 15.0 versus 31.1 percent in a third (p = 0.001), with less transfusion, so the exposure is confounded with the extent of surgery, and the stratified analysis the authors say addresses this is reported only as data not shown",
      "Several of the sensitivity analyses that support the robustness claim, including the QUIPS low-versus-moderate-to-high comparison and the anatomic-resection strata, are reported as data not shown and cannot be checked",
      "Four different constructs are pooled as one exposure: a gradient of 10 mmHg or more, portal vein pressure of 20 cmH2O or more, the presence of gastro-oesophageal varices, and platelets below 100,000 with a spleen above 12 cm; the prevalence of the resulting exposure ranges from 21.7 to 51.7 percent across studies",
      "No funnel plot, Egger test or any formal assessment of small-study or publication bias is presented, in an analysis whose most extreme subgroup estimates come from its smallest studies",
      "The search covered MEDLINE only, in English only, with no grey literature, no registries and no non-English reports; four full texts could not be obtained and were excluded; only 2 of 11 studies are Asian, and the principal dissenting Asian study was eligible for the survival analysis alone",
      "The one study showing no effect of portal hypertension on 3- or 5-year mortality is the only multicentre study in the set, and the paper offers no examination of why the largest and least selected cohort is the discordant one",
      "Two of the included studies come from the same unit over overlapping years (1989 to 1997 and 1991 to 1994), and the stated rule against duplicate cohorts is satisfied by entering one into the survival pool and the other into the decompensation pool, which conceals rather than removes the overlap",
      "The senior author declares consultancy and grants from Bayer and relationships with nine other companies, and the practical consequence of the recommendation is to move patients with portal hypertension from resection to transplantation, ablation or chemoembolisation, the last of which the Discussion endorses by citing the group's own drug-eluting-bead series"
    ],
    "n": "11 studies with 1,737 patients with cirrhosis and HCC treated surgically; 1,572 patients (574 with and 998 without clinically significant portal hypertension) in the survival analysis with 491 deaths at 3 years and 694 at 5 years, and 1,108 patients (386 with and 722 without) with 197 decompensation events",
    "bottom_line": "Pools 11 observational studies and finds that clinically significant portal hypertension roughly doubles 3- and 5-year mortality after resection for HCC (pooled OR 2.09 and 2.07) and triples the odds of postoperative decompensation (OR 3.04). Every estimate is crude and unadjusted, portal hypertension is a marker of more advanced cirrhosis, and the dramatic subgroup figures that justify measuring the hepatic venous pressure gradient come from three small studies totalling 115 patients, two of them the authors' own.",
    "funding": "Supported by Instituto de Salud Carlos III grants PI11/01830 to Bruix and FIS 13/00341 to Bosch, and by FEDER; CIBERehd is funded by the Instituto de Salud Carlos III. Bruix declares consultancy, advisory roles and grants from Bayer and relationships with BioCompatibles, Novartis, Daichi, Arqule, Abbott, Bristol-Myers Squibb, GlaxoSmithKline, Kowa, Lilly and Roche"
  },
  "27248425": {
    "kind": "cohort",
    "limitations": [
      "Retrospective analysis, although the database was prospectively collected",
      "The risk stratification was never externally validated, only internally cross-validated by 10-fold cross-validation",
      "Surgical indications and tumour burden expanded over the 14-year study period",
      "The authors acknowledge that definitions of postoperative decompensation vary widely between series, so their 19.9 percent rate is not comparable with others",
      "The authors attribute the discrepancy between the random-forest variable ranking and the partitioning tree to the difference between the two methods",
      "The authors predict the risk within each class will fall as hepatitis C is cured, so the absolute rates may overstate current risk"

    "critique": [
      "The high-risk class contains 20 patients with 12 events, no confidence interval is given for its 60.0 percent decompensation rate or its 25.0 percent liver-related mortality (5 of 20), and 20 is exactly the minimum node size the tree was permitted to split at, so the class was created at the algorithm's own stopping boundary",
      "The intermediate class holds 297 of 543 patients (54.7 percent) and merges three clinically unlike groups, no portal hypertension with a major resection, portal hypertension with a minor resection, and a minor resection with a MELD above 9, into a single 28.6 percent figure that cannot inform a decision about any of them",

      "The paediatric statements are new and were voted by the same faculty, with paediatric hepatologists added to only some panels and the composition of the vote for each statement not reported.       "The statement an HCC board needs most is the one without a number.       "The grey zone between the rule-out (liver stiffness 15 kPa or less with platelets 150 x 10^9/L or more) and the rule-in (25 kPa or more) is handled by ANTICIPATE at a 60% probability of clinically significant portal hypertension, as a weak B.2 recommendation.     "25014687": {
      "label": "CLARINET",
      "design": "RCT",
      "arms": "Lanreotide vs placebo",
      "result": "Primary endpoint met: median PFS not reached vs 18.0 mo (HR 0.47, 95% CI 0.30-0.73); 24-mo PFS 65.1% vs 33.0%; no OS or QoL difference",
      "caution": "96% stable; grade 2 HR 0.45 (0.22–0.91), pancreatic HR 0.58 (0.32–1.04); no predictive cutoff",
      "quotes": [
        "204 patients with unresectable or metastatic, somatostatin-receptor-positive, grade 1 or 2 (Ki-67 under 10%) non-functioning enteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours randomised at 48 centres in 14 countries between June 2006 and April 2013: 101 to lanreotide Autogel 120 mg and 103 to placebo, with 96% having had no documented progression in the preceding 3 to 6 months.",
        "CLARINET establishes that lanreotide 120 mg delays radiographic progression in somatostatin-receptor-positive, grade 1 or 2 enteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours, with a hazard ratio of 0.47 (95% CI 0.30–0.73) and 65.1% versus 33.0% progression-free at 24 months, and it does so across hepatic tumour volumes above and below 25%. What it does not establish is that this changes anything a patient feels or how long they live: no statistically significant difference in overall survival or quality of life was demonstrated, the population was non-functioning and 96% radiographically stable at entry, and subgroup estimates do not establish a predictive grade threshold; grade 2 HR was 0.45 (95% CI 0.22–0.91). The placebo arm ran a median 18.0 months without progression, which is the figure to carry into any discussion of whether to start treatment now or watch, and the hepatic-volume subgroup everyone quotes was collapsed from five prespecified categories to two after the data were in.",
        "The subgroup that matters most for liver-directed decisions is a post hoc construction. Hepatic tumour volume was prespecified in five categories whose estimated hazard ratios ranged from 0.24 to 0.54, and was collapsed after the fact into a dichotomy at 25%. The conclusion that the effect holds irrespective of hepatic tumour volume rests on that simplification, as the paper's own table footnote states.",
        "CLARINET’s grade 2 subgroup HR was 0.45 (95% CI 0.22–0.91). The HR 0.58 (0.32–1.04) belongs to the pancreatic-primary subgroup. Subgroup estimates do not establish differential benefit by grade or primary site.",
        "CLARINET subgroup estimates are exploratory: the pancreatic subgroup HR was 0.58 (95% CI 0.32–1.04), hepatic tumour volume >25% HR 0.45 (0.23–0.88), and grade 2 HR 0.45 (0.22–0.91). These are different strata. The estimates do not establish a predictive primary-site, grade or liver-volume cutoff.",
        "The whole benefit is radiographic. Overall survival did not differ, EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status did not differ, and the population was non-functioning by design so there were no hormonal symptoms to improve. Crossover is invoked to explain the survival null without any crossover numbers or a sensitivity analysis being presented.",
        "The size of the effect is unknown because the trial ended before it could be measured. Median progression-free survival was not reached with lanreotide within the 96-week fixed study duration, so the delay is known only to exceed the observation window, and the 96-week design cannot address how long treatment should continue.",
        "Progression-free survival and time to tumour progression return the identical 18.0-month placebo median from different event counts (60 against 58), which shows the median sits in a sparse region of the curve where two events make no difference to the estimate.",
        "The chromogranin A result is reported on 64 of 101 and 64 of 103 patients, roughly two-thirds of each arm, with no account of the missing third, and it is a biochemical change in a non-functioning tumour population where it carries no symptomatic meaning.",
        "Enrolment required somatostatin-receptor scintigraphy uptake of grade 2 or higher within the previous 6 months, so the trial selected the patients most likely to respond and says nothing about receptor-poor disease, which is precisely the group in whom embolisation, chemotherapy or resection is being weighed.",
        "The trial excluded any prior radionuclide therapy at any time, chemoembolisation or chemotherapy within 6 months, and more than 15 days of previous somatostatin analogue. The cohort is therefore essentially naive to liver-directed treatment, and nothing in the result informs sequencing with embolisation, radioembolisation or PRRT.",
        "The discussion raises the obvious reading of its own data, that an 18-month placebo median supports watchful waiting, and sets it aside on the ground that the study examined prevention of progression. That is a restatement of the trial's design, not an answer to the question of whether delaying treatment costs the patient anything.",
        "The adverse events that matter for a surgical population are presented as reassurance. Cholelithiasis occurred in 10% against 3% and hyperglycaemia in 5% against 0%, and the serious treatment-related events in the lanreotide arm include biliary fistula and cholelithiasis, in patients who may later need hepatectomy or arterial therapy; the discussion calls the safety profile favourable by comparison with targeted agents and chemotherapy.",
        "The sponsor controlled the trial end to end. Ipsen, which markets lanreotide, designed, funded and conducted the study; the contract research organisation's statisticians worked under the oversight of the sponsor's own biostatistics department; a medical writer paid by the sponsor drafted the manuscript; and one co-author is affiliated to Ipsen.",
        "Two letters in the New England Journal of Medicine with an author reply are linked to this paper in PubMed (PMIDs 25317882, 25317883 and 25317881). The full texts could not be obtained, so no point above draws on them and whatever objections they raise are not represented here.",
        "Start a somatostatin analogue for antiproliferative effect and symptom control.",
        "Standard",
        "A",
        "Receptor-positive or functional phenotypes, and anyone in whom progression would be hard to salvage. PROMID (n=85, treatment-naive midgut) gave time to progression 14.3 versus 6.0 months, hazard ratio 0.34 (95% CI 0.20–0.59); CLARINET (n=204, non-functioning enteropancreatic, Ki-67 under 10%) gave a progression-free survival hazard ratio of 0.47 (0.30–0.73) with 24-month progression-free survival 65.1% versus 33.0%.",
        "Do not make it mandatory for every patient. Grade A applies to the antiproliferative indication in unresectable disease: PROMID and CLARINET enrolled only patients with no curative option, unresectable disease or declined surgery. In resectable or ablatable disease, analogue versus resection or ablation is an MDT decision.",
        "Neither trial established an overall-survival benefit — CLARINET found no significant difference in overall survival or quality of life, and PROMID is an interim analysis at 67 progressions and 16 deaths of a trial that enrolled 85 of a planned 162 patients and was then closed for slow accrual, so its confirmatory survival analysis at 121 deaths was never performed. The effect is stabilisation, not shrinkage: one partial remission per arm in PROMID, and objective remissions with an analogue are rare. For a liver pathway the decisive limitation is that PROMID's exploratory burden subgroups had imprecise estimates and did not establish a predictive liver-volume threshold — hazard ratio 0.17 (0.08–0.40) at 0 to 10% hepatic involvement, 0.40 (0.10–1.67) at 10 to 50% and 0.71 (0.11–4.45) above 50%, with 95% of patients having Ki-67 of 2% or less and 64/85 (75%) having 10% or less liver involvement, including those without liver disease. CLARINET held across hepatic volume, hazard ratio 0.45 (0.23–0.88) above 25%, but that dichotomy is a post hoc simplification of a prespecified five-category variable whose component hazard ratios ran 0.24 to 0.54. For carcinoid-syndrome control the source is ENETS 2024, not these trials.",
        "Continue the somatostatin analogue for functional-syndrome control where it is needed, and after clinically significant progression in a nonfunctional tumour do not automatically continue it for antiproliferative benefit.",
        "C",
        "Functional disease, where the analogue is doing hormonal work that nothing else in the plan replaces.",
        "Carrying an analogue indefinitely in a nonfunctional tumour that has progressed on it, on the assumption that it is still holding the tumour back.",
        "Downgraded to C: this is a position taken in the absence of evidence rather than from it.         "Do not continue a somatostatin analogue for antiproliferative benefit in every nonfunctional NET after significant progression.",
        "Avoid",
        "B",
        "Continue it for hormonal control where the tumour is functional.",
        "PROMID and CLARINET tested delay of progression in stable, indolent disease — 96% of CLARINET patients had no progression in the 3 to 6 months before randomisation — and neither establishes an antiproliferative role after documented progression.",
        "Octreotide LAR or lanreotide",
        "PROMID: time to progression 14.3 versus 6 months with octreotide versus placebo in midgut NET. CLARINET established PFS benefit with lanreotide in nonfunctional enteropancreatic NET, Ki-67 <10%.",
        "CLARINET randomized double-blind trial, 204 nonfunctioning advanced enteropancreatic NET patients (101 lanreotide, 103 placebo).",
        "From randomization, median PFS not reached with lanreotide versus 18 months placebo; HR 0.47 (95% CI 0.30–0.73). Twenty-four-month PFS 65.1% versus 33.0%. No significant OS or QoL difference in the primary report. Diarrhea 26% versus 9%.",

      "design": "RCT",
      "arms": "Lanreotide vs placebo",
      "result": "Primary endpoint met: median PFS not reached vs 18.0 mo (HR 0.47, 95% CI 0.30-0.73); 24-mo PFS 65.1% vs 33.0%; no OS or QoL difference",

      "quotes": [
        "204 patients with unresectable or metastatic, somatostatin-receptor-positive, grade 1 or 2 (Ki-67 under 10%) non-functioning enteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours randomised at 48 centres in 14 countries between June 2006 and April 2013: 101 to lanreotide Autogel 120 mg and 103 to placebo, with 96% having had no documented progression in the preceding 3 to 6 months.",
        "CLARINET establishes that lanreotide 120 mg delays radiographic progression in somatostatin-receptor-positive, grade 1 or 2 enteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours, with a hazard ratio of 0.47 (95% CI 0.30–0.73) and 65.1% versus 33.0% progression-free at 24 months, and it does so across hepatic tumour volumes above and below 25%. What it does not establish is that this changes anything a patient feels or how long they live: no statistically significant difference in overall survival or quality of life was demonstrated, the population was non-functioning and 96% radiographically stable at entry, and subgroup estimates do not establish a predictive grade threshold; grade 2 HR was 0.45 (95% CI 0.22–0.91). The placebo arm ran a median 18.0 months without progression, which is the figure to carry into any discussion of whether to start treatment now or watch, and the hepatic-volume subgroup everyone quotes was collapsed from five prespecified categories to two after the data were in.",
        "The subgroup that matters most for liver-directed decisions is a post hoc construction. Hepatic tumour volume was prespecified in five categories whose estimated hazard ratios ranged from 0.24 to 0.54, and was collapsed after the fact into a dichotomy at 25%. The conclusion that the effect holds irrespective of hepatic tumour volume rests on that simplification, as the paper's own table footnote states.",
        "CLARINET’s grade 2 subgroup HR was 0.45 (95% CI 0.22–0.91). The HR 0.58 (0.32–1.04) belongs to the pancreatic-primary subgroup. Subgroup estimates do not establish differential benefit by grade or primary site.",
        "CLARINET subgroup estimates are exploratory: the pancreatic subgroup HR was 0.58 (95% CI 0.32–1.04), hepatic tumour volume >25% HR 0.45 (0.23–0.88), and grade 2 HR 0.45 (0.22–0.91). These are different strata. The estimates do not establish a predictive primary-site, grade or liver-volume cutoff.",
        "The whole benefit is radiographic. Overall survival did not differ, EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status did not differ, and the population was non-functioning by design so there were no hormonal symptoms to improve. Crossover is invoked to explain the survival null without any crossover numbers or a sensitivity analysis being presented.",
        "The size of the effect is unknown because the trial ended before it could be measured.         "Progression-free survival and time to tumour progression return the identical 18.0-month placebo median from different event counts (60 against 58), which shows the median sits in a sparse region of the curve where two events make no difference to the estimate.",
        "The chromogranin A result is reported on 64 of 101 and 64 of 103 patients, roughly two-thirds of each arm, with no account of the missing third, and it is a biochemical change in a non-functioning tumour population where it carries no symptomatic meaning.",
        "Enrolment required somatostatin-receptor scintigraphy uptake of grade 2 or higher within the previous 6 months, so the trial selected the patients most likely to respond and says nothing about receptor-poor disease, which is precisely the group in whom embolisation, chemotherapy or resection is being weighed.",
        "The trial excluded any prior radionuclide therapy at any time, chemoembolisation or chemotherapy within 6 months, and more than 15 days of previous somatostatin analogue. The cohort is therefore essentially naive to liver-directed treatment, and nothing in the result informs sequencing with embolisation, radioembolisation or PRRT.",
        "The discussion raises the obvious reading of its own data, that an 18-month placebo median supports watchful waiting, and sets it aside on the ground that the study examined prevention of progression.         "The adverse events that matter for a surgical population are presented as reassurance.         "The sponsor controlled the trial end to end. Ipsen, which markets lanreotide, designed, funded and conducted the study; the contract research organisation's statisticians worked under the oversight of the sponsor's own biostatistics department; a medical writer paid by the sponsor drafted the manuscript; and one co-author is affiliated to Ipsen.",
        "Two letters in the New England Journal of Medicine with an author reply are linked to this paper in PubMed (PMIDs 25317882, 25317883 and 25317881). The full texts could not be obtained, so no point above draws on them and whatever objections they raise are not represented here.",
        "Start a somatostatin analogue for antiproliferative effect and symptom control.",

        "Do not make it mandatory for every patient.         "Neither trial established an overall-survival benefit — CLARINET found no significant difference in overall survival or quality of life, and PROMID is an interim analysis at 67 progressions and 16 deaths of a trial that enrolled 85 of a planned 162 patients and was then closed for slow accrual, so its confirmatory survival analysis at 121 deaths was never performed.         "Continue the somatostatin analogue for functional-syndrome control where it is needed, and after clinically significant progression in a nonfunctional tumour do not automatically continue it for antiproliferative benefit.",

files.old: "Single-arm data only, and the endpoints are imaging. RASER treated 29 patients with a solitary tumour of 3 cm or less: target-lesion complete response in 24 of 29 (83%), a sustained complete response after one treatment in 26 of 29 (90%), target-lesion progression in 3 of 29 (10%) and overall progression in 9 of 29 (31%) at a median follow-up of 691 days, read by one unblinded in-house radiologist with no comparator and 5 of 29 (17%) lost to follow-up. All 8 explants showed 100% necrosis of the target lesion, but 3 of those 8 livers held additional untreated HCC, one with vascular invasion. LEGACY is retrospective, 162 patients, median tumour 2.7 cm with 62% under 3 cm: best response of 88.3% (95% CI 82.4 to 92.4) by localised mRECIST falls to a confirmed 46.3% (38.8 to 54.0) by RECIST 1.1, and 45 patients (28%) went on to transplant or resection, so its 86.6% 3-year survival cannot be attributed to the radiation. Both studies were funded by the microsphere manufacturer.",
files.new: "Evidence includes single-arm imaging outcomes and selected surgical pathology. Gabr 2021 (PMID 32749512) found complete necrosis in 30/45 specimens (67%), including 11/11 after >400 Gy to the perfused segment; the cohort includes only patients who reached transplant or resection. RASER treated 29 patients with a solitary tumour of 3 cm or less: target-lesion complete response in 24 of 29 (83%), a sustained complete response after one treatment in 26 of 29 (90%), target-lesion progression in 3 of 29 (10%) and overall progression in 9 of 29 (31%) at a median follow-up of 691 days, read by one unblinded in-house radiologist with no comparator and 5 of 29 (17%) lost to follow-up. All 8 explants showed 100% necrosis of the target lesion, but 3 of those 8 livers held additional untreated HCC, one with vascular invasion. LEGACY is retrospective, 162 patients, median tumour 2.7 cm with 62% under 3 cm: best response of 88.3% (95% CI 82.4 to 92.4) by localised mRECIST falls to a confirmed 46.3% (38.8 to 54.0) by RECIST 1.1, and 45 patients (28%) went on to transplant or resection, so its 86.6% 3-year survival cannot be attributed to the radiation. Both studies were funded by the microsphere manufacturer.",

files.old:
"Selected segmentectomy to one or two segments can be definitive curative-intent therapy. The strongest prospective evidence is solitary HCC ≤3 cm; selected retrospective cohorts extend to larger tumours, but ≤8 cm is not a universal curative cutoff. RASER (29 patients) reported 90% sustained complete response; LEGACY (162) supports response durability but includes later surgery and transplant. NCCN specifies >400 Gy to ≤25% of liver in Child-Pugh A — document dose compartment and microsphere model. Segment absorbed dose is not interchangeable with tumour absorbed dose. Lobar Y-90 for broader burden is generally control or conversion: do not transfer segmentectomy curative claims to all Y-90.",
  ["33739462","35617978"],["DOSIMETRY","EXPERTISE","PAYER"]],
